To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biosilica of diatoms can be used as an immobilization matrix for a variety of multimeric and cofactor-dependent enzymes, and that the biosilicate of diatoms can serve as a novel negative selection marker in diatom genetic engineering.

we have engineered diatoms to express and incorporate into their silica cell wall a variety of complex enzymes, and that this approach is applicable to a wide range of enzymes and can be utilized as a negative selection marker for genetic engineering in diatoms.
we have developed a novel method for the production of functionalized silica materials by genetic engineering of living diatoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic engineering of the diatom silica biomineralization system.
the development of a novel approach to produce biomineral-based, functional materials in vivo by genetic engineering of living diatoms.
the development of a novel, general, and highly effective approach for in vivo production of functional materials based on biomineralization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in vivo incorporation of enzymes into biosilica is a versatile approach to produce functional enzyme-based materials in vivo.
the in vivo immobilization approach is a general and powerful method to produce functional materials in living cells.
diatom-based in vivo immobilization is a versatile and robust approach to immobilize multimeric and redox-active enzymes in a biomineral matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diatom biosynthetic pathway for silica production is a versatile platform for functional protein immobilization and that the diatom system is a promising tool for the production of functional biomimetic materials.
the diatom silica immobilization approach can be extended to a wide range of enzymes and is a promising platform for the production of functional materials.
the cellular machinery for diatom silica formation can be engineered to incorporate a broad variety of “simple” and “complex” enzymes into the biosilicification pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in vivo immobilization approach is a general and versatile method to incorporate a wide variety of enzymes into diatom silica and that it is applicable to the production of a broad variety of functional materials.
the diatom-based system can be used to produce biomineral-based materials with complex functionalities.
the in vivo approach to immobilization of enzymes is not limited to monomeric enzymes with simple activity requirements.
